text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Fuel prices may rise in Portugal in October if international oil markets remain buoyant this week.

- The Portuguese government expects to post a loss of around 1.6 billion escudos from the production of Clio cars at its factory in Setubal between July and December 1998, a source close to the process told the paper.
- The government is to invest 200 billion escudos in railway infrastructure in 1997.
- Centre-right Social Democratic Party (PSD) refuses coalition with rightwing Popular Party (PP) in the next local authority elections in 1997.
- The Portuguese invested 28.63 billion escudos abroad in the first five months of 1996, 11.45 percent up from the same year-ago period, reveals a Bank of Portugal study.
- Left-wing trade union group CGTP wants the 1997 budget to cut workers' taxes.
- Pulp company Portucel was the most active share on Lisbon stock exchange yesterday. A company official said Portucel expected to raise hardwood pulp prices in October.
